## Result

`workspace.dsl` defines **one view** — the `SystemContext` view of the `Library` system. I rendered it to:

- **`/work/SystemContext.svg`** (920×420)

It shows the C4 system context: **Patron** (Person, teal `#0E7490`) → **Library** (System, blue `#1168BD`), with the relationship *"Browses the catalogue through"* `[HTTPS]`. The two containers (Catalog Web App, Circulation Service) are intentionally not shown, since a system-context view only depicts the system and its external actors — matching what the parsed model reports.

## How I got there (and one caveat)

The `structurizr` tooling only exports views to **text** (PlantUML / C4-PlantUML / Mermaid) — it doesn't produce images. To turn that into an image I'd normally run a renderer, but this environment has:

- **No internet** (DNS fails, external hosts unreachable), and
- **No local renderers** — no `plantuml`, `mmdc`, `java`, `node`, `python3`, `dot`, `inkscape`, or `imagemagick`, and no SVG→PNG converter.

So I generated the **C4-style SVG directly from the parsed model** (standard C4 colors, person icon, labeled relationship) rather than via PlantUML/Mermaid. That's why the output is **SVG, not PNG** — there's no converter available to rasterize it.

If you'd prefer PNG, or want the diagram produced by the actual PlantUML/Mermaid pipeline, I can do that in an environment with network access or a renderer installed — just let me know. I can also add the other view types (e.g., a container view for `Library`) if you want more than the single context view.
